name: Verner Osgood
summary: Outside Lakeshire’s smithy, Verner Osgood keeps the forge at work. He must meet the Stormwind Guard’s need for horseshoes, weapons, and armor while gnolls raid the hills.

sections.title: The Anvil of Lakeshire
sections.body: Verner Osgood keeps Lakeshire’s forge working, making horseshoes and other supplies for the town. The Stormwind Guard continually requisitions his stock for weapons and armor. With the kingdom’s forces stretched thin and local garrisons short on supplies, Verner bears much of the burden of equipping Redridge’s defenders.

sections.title: A Plague of Gnolls
sections.body: Gnoll raids threaten Verner’s work and the town’s horses. Packs ambush livestock in the Redridge hills and seize working horses that stray beyond Lakeshire. Verner recruits travelers to hunt the marauders and their packleader, Yowler.

faq.answer: Verner Osgood tends Lakeshire’s forge, making metalwork and horseshoes while meeting the local garrison’s heavy demands for equipment.

faq.q: Why is Verner low on horseshoes and iron?
faq.answer: Iron supplies are continually requisitioned for weapons and armor for the Stormwind Guard in Redridge. Verner has barely enough metal left to shoe the town’s horses.

faq.q: What problem does Verner have with the gnolls?
faq.answer: Gnoll raiders near Lakeshire seize Verner’s horses when they stray beyond town. He hires travelers to protect his livelihood and hunt the packs in retribution.

faq.q: Who is Yowler and why does Verner want him dead?
faq.answer: Yowler leads the local gnoll packs in the hills. Verner wants him slain to break the raiders’ coordination and stop them from terrorizing the town and killing his horses.

faq.q: What is Verner's connection to Magistrate Solomon?
faq.answer: Verner works under Magistrate Solomon’s civic authority in Lakeshire. He balances his craft for civilians with the civic and military needs of the magistrate’s beleaguered administration.

faq.q: Does Verner have family in Stormwind?
faq.answer: Verner shares his surname with Stormwind tradesmen Donal and Basil Osgood. Their shared name suggests an established lineage of working-class human craftsmen across the region.

angles.text: As a blacksmith, Verner shoes civilian horses while meeting the harsh quotas imposed for garrison defense.
Lakeshire depends on local craftsmen like Verner to endure while Stormwind’s military aid remains dangerously constrained.
As a human, you share the resilience of Stormwind’s common folk, holding ground against gnolls and shortages alike.
